chunks: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarkhasi, in Sarakhs, told us: Abu Lubaid Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami told us: Hashim ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makhzumi told us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam told us, from Yahya ibn Ayub, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Abd Allah ibn Mashruh, from Rabia' ibn Bawra', from Fadala ibn Ubaid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:
Whoever desires the Treasure of Hadith, upon him is (to adhere to): 'There is no force, nor strength, except in Allah'.

key_terms.كَنْزَ الْحَدِيثِ: Treasure of Hadith (profound knowledge or essence of traditions)
key_terms.لَا حَوْلٍ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no force, nor strength, except in Allah (a key dhikr phrase)

ai.seo_question: What is the 'Treasure of Hadith' and how does one acquire it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to emphasize that true mastery of prophetic traditions (*Hadith*) is not merely intellectual but spiritual, requiring divine assistance. The phrase 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' serves as the essential key to unlocking this 'treasure,' linking the acquisition of sacred knowledge directly to reliance on Allah’s power. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that knowledge is a light granted by God, accessible through spiritual devotion and remembrance.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abu Nasr, Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Tamim al-Sarkhasi, in Sarakhs, that he said: We were told by Abu Lubaid, Muhammed bin Idris al-Shami, that he said: We were told by Hashim bin Abdul-Aziz al-Makhzoumi, that he said: We were told by Sa’eed bin Abi Maryam, from Yahya bin Ayoub, from Khalid bin Yazid, from Abdullah bin Mashrouh, from Rabee’a bin Bawra’, from Fadala bin Ubaid, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:
The one who wants the Treasure of Speech, upon him is (to adhere to): «There is no force, nor strength, except in Allah».
